subject.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config

question: Should OpenClaw remove the shipped `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` config value now using this doctor migration, or preserve the enum until a longer deprecation or real gRPC exporter path exists?
rationale: The code path is coherent, but removing a shipped config value changes upgrade behavior for existing configs and requires maintainer intent about the compatibility contract.

options.title: Accept the doctor-backed contract change
options.body: Keep the stricter schema and doctor migration if maintainers agree that `grpc` was shipped but nonfunctional and that preserving no-export semantics is the right upgrade path.

options.title: Keep grpc during a deprecation window
options.body: Preserve `grpc` in validation and improve warnings/docs if maintainers want existing configs to keep passing before a later removal.

options.title: Pause for real gRPC support
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers prefer implementing the larger gRPC exporter path instead of removing the config value now.

recommendation.title: Accept the doctor-backed contract change
recommendation.body: Keep the stricter schema and doctor migration if maintainers agree that `grpc` was shipped but nonfunctional and that preserving no-export semantics is the right upgrade path.

likelyOwner.reason: The original diagnostics OTel config/runtime surface traces to `5c4079f66cc0`, making this the best available owner for the compatibility-direction choice.
